chose: Thread model with a deterministic resume-or-refresh rule in the coordinator. A task's conversation is resumed (claude --resume / --fork-session, codex resume) only when the gap since its last turn is inside the prompt-cache TTL and the work left is short: a verify_failed fix, a merge-conflict fix, or a park whose wait resolved. Otherwise the task gets a fresh session with the 3.3 packet. The 3.7 levers cut what a resume costs.
over: Always resuming a task's thread (the Claude Code Projects and Managed Agents workflow shape), or never resuming (today's fresh session per task)
because: Per-turn cost scales with the context carried. A resumed thread re-reads its whole history on every turn. That is cheap only while the cache is warm, since cache reads cost a tenth of fresh input; a cold resume re-writes the whole prefix at the cache-write premium. A fresh session starts small but pays to rediscover. 1.1 shows both sides: session 032d1bdd peaked at 266k and failed verify, and the fresh retry 17c753a6 rebuilt to 157k. Resuming pays only for short, warm work on the same context. The rule is code, so sofar still makes zero model calls.
